headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0076 — SMTO couldn't save the clipboard picture as a file

html:
SMTO-EXE-0076 — SMTO couldn't save the clipboard picture as a file

GUID: f219ef93-5f5f-5e4d-bff4-2ab598e19738
Slug: clipboard-artifact-failure
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • SMTO tried to save the picture on the clipboard as an image file for this Task, but couldn't store it. Your clipboard wasn't changed and no partial image file was kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Send the request as a normal message in a Conversation, so it runs as part of a Task. SMTO saves clipboard pictures into the current Task's files; without a Task it has nowhere to put the image.
  2. On the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer), make sure the disk has free space. The picture is written to that computer's disk, so a full disk stops the save.
  3. If you manage that computer, check that the account running the Gateway can write to its SMTO folder (by default .smto/artifacts in that account's home folder). A folder the Gateway isn't allowed to write to causes the same failure.
  4. Ask SMTO to read the clipboard picture again. Reading the clipboard doesn't change it, so trying again is safe once the cause is fixed.

What success looks like

  • The Task finishes and shows a saved PNG image of the picture that was on the clipboard.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer, saying which computer you used. Don't paste the clipboard picture itself into the report; it may be private.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's clipboard read_image failed because the request had no run/conversation scope or writing the PNG into the run's Gateway artifact directory failed.

What this means

  • Image export lacked an owning run/conversation scope or failed while publishing the captured image into the Gateway artifact workspace. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Image export lacked an owning run/conversation scope or failed while publishing the captured image into the Gateway artifact workspace.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect run/conversation identity and the existing artifact publication result; a storage failure does not prove the clipboard was empty.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the clipboard.read_image ClipboardRequest carries both conversation_id and run_id (from _artifact_scope or the execution context). On the Gateway, check that GATEWAY_ARTIFACT_ROOT (default ~/.smto/artifacts) exists, is writable by the Gateway account and has free space for the run's files directory, then issue a new explicit read_image.
  • Use an active run with a writable Gateway artifact workspace and inspect artifact storage availability.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use an active run with a writable Gateway artifact workspace and inspect artifact storage availability.

How to verify the fix

  • The explicit image read produces a valid artifact attached to the intended run.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
